item.title: [Recap] Derik Queen (NOP): Derik Queen notched 16 points (4-of-8 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds and three blocks in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Derik Queen notched 16 points (4-of-8 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), four rebounds and three blocks in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.

Queen did most of his damage offensively in the second quarter, scoring eight of his 16 points. However, of greater importance to fantasy managers may be the three blocks, a new season-high and two shy of the second-year forward/center’s career high. However, his defense remains a work in progress, even with the blocks recorded on Monday. While Queen has been a consistently productive option for fantasy managers, the defensive issues are why he’s averaging 22 minutes per game and not more.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jeremiah Fears (NOP): Jeremiah Fears accounted for 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Jeremiah Fears accounted for 11 points (4-of-12 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, eight assists, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.

Fears led the Pelicans with eight assists, but he also recorded six turnovers in Monday’s 138-87 defeat. This was one of his poorer performances of the season, and the Pelicans not having Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson didn’t help either. Fears will look to bounce back on Wednesday when the Pelicans host the Nets. That should be a better matchup for him than the red-hot Warriors were.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Dejounte Murray (NOP): Dejounte Murray tallied 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.
item.description:
Dejounte Murray tallied 12 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Warriors.

The Pelicans didn’t have Trey Murphy or Zion Williamson on Monday, and those absences were certainly felt. Murray shot a solid percentage from the field and led the Pelicans starters in scoring, but it wasn’t enough when the Warriors knocked down 21 three-pointers. Murray has been close to a top-50 player in nine-cat formats, but it’s fair to wonder if his presence in the lineup has limited Jeremiah Fears’ fantasy ceiling. That’s something to watch as the season progresses.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] De'Anthony Melton (GSW): De’Anthony Melton amassed 16 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
item.description:
De’Anthony Melton amassed 16 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.

Melton was one of four Warriors to make at least four three-pointers in Monday’s blowout victory. With Brandon Williams suffering a hamstring injury in the first quarter, Melton is one Warrior whose minutes may increase if Williams misses time. Currently a player who should be rostered in deep leagues, some managers in 12-team leagues may be willing to roll the dice on Melton in the short term.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg produced 23 points (8-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.

Lendeborg continues to shine for the Warriors, making all four of his three-point attempts on Monday. The rookie forward has scored at least 20 points in six of 11 games and is considered by many to be one of the early favorites for Rookie of the Year. The Warriors play two more games this week, at Houston and San Antonio, so we’ll learn a bit more about Lendeborg in games of that magnitude.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski amassed 25 points (10-of-19 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski amassed 25 points (10-of-19 FGs), two rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.

Podziemski shot 5-of-11 from beyond the arc on Monday, a season high for three-pointers in a game for the fourth-year guard. Even better for fantasy managers, Podz recorded a complete stat line, his third in as many games. Based on his ADP, Podziemski wasn’t expected to be a top-100 player this season. However, while it is early, he’s been a top-75 player in nine-cat formats.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Stephen Curry (GSW): Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.
item.description:
Stephen Curry tallied 25 points (6-of-10 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pelicans.

Curry only played 21 minutes in Monday’s blowout victory, none in the fourth quarter. That’s all the time he needed to notch another career milestone, as the Warriors guard moved past DeMar DeRozan into 16th place on the NBA’s all-time scoring list. Thus far, Curry’s production has exceeded his preseason ADP by a safe distance, as he’s been a top-5 player in nine-cat formats. The Warriors end their week with games against the Rockets and Spurs, two teams that should offer up greater resistance than the Pelicans did.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Dillon Brooks (PHX): Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with seven points (3-of-14 FGs), four rebounds and one three-pointer.
item.description:
Dillon Brooks finished Monday’s loss to the Spurs with seven points (3-of-14 FGs), four rebounds and one three-pointer.

While Devin Booker scored 32 points, no other Suns starter scored more than seven in Monday’s 122-96 defeat. Brooks had an especially rough night, as he shot 2-of-12 from inside the three-point line. While he managed a few rebounds, his poor shooting was compounded by a lack of assists and defensive stats. Brooks will look to bounce back on Tuesday against the Clippers.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.
item.description:
Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.

Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Onyeka Okongwu (ATL): Onyeka Okongwu posted 16 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Onyeka Okongwu posted 16 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.

Okongwu was one of the bright spots for Atlanta in this one as he got off to an excellent start, knocking down a pair of three-pointers as part of a nine-point outburst in the opening stanza. He’s reached double-digit points in five consecutive games since the start of November and is averaging over 16 points and nine rebounds during that span. The Hawks will attempt to get back on track when the face the Bulls in a road matchup on Friday.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler delivered 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
item.description:
Walker Kessler delivered 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in Monday’s win over the Hawks.

Kessler got off to an outstanding start with 15 first-half points and he managed to pull down just enough rebounds to notch a double-double for the seventh consecutive game since late October. The 25-year-old big man has fit seamlessly into Los Angeles’ nucleus after missing nearly all of last season following shoulder surgery.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Nickeil Alexander-Walker (ATL): Nickeil Alexander-Walker tallied 20 points (6-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks over 34 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Nickeil Alexander-Walker tallied 20 points (6-of-19 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks over 34 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.

Alexander-Walker has been a consistent scoring threat for fantasy managers, scoring at least 20 points on eight occasions this season. He’s accomplished the feat in seven of his last eight games since October 28. He would’ve had an even bigger scoring performance had he not gone just 4-of-14 from three-point range in this one. The Hawks are back in action with a road matchup against the Bulls on Friday.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Sandro Mamukelashvili (LAL): Sandro Mamukelashvili chipped in 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block over 32 minutes off the bench in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
item.description:
Sandro Mamukelashvili chipped in 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block over 32 minutes off the bench in Monday’s win over the Hawks.

Mamukelashvili saw a massive uptick in minutes and offensive opportunities with Austin Reaves sitting out due to illness on the tail-end of a back-to-back for the Lakers. The 27-year-old drained 5-of-8 shots from three-point range and established season-high marks in both minutes and points. His fantasy appeal is strictly limited to situation-dependent matchups like this one where he receives extra chances.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jarrett Allen (CLE): Jarrett Allen producted 12 points (5-of-5 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
item.description:
Jarrett Allen producted 12 points (5-of-5 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, one assist, one block and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.

One of the few positives for the Cavaliers on Monday was that Allen hit his third three-pointer of the season. By comparison, he shot 3-for-41 from deep over his prior five seasons. Allen isn’t going to become a face-up center anytime soon, so there’s no need to entertain what that could do for his fantasy value. But he didn’t miss a shot from the field on Monday, which is a positive for fantasy managers rostering him.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Meleek Thomas (CLE): Meleek Thomas finished Monday’s loss to the Hornets with 18 points (7-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers.
item.description:
Meleek Thomas finished Monday’s loss to the Hornets with 18 points (7-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers.

With Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson benching his starters for the entire fourth quarter, reserves like Thomas took on larger roles. The rookie wing scored 12 of his 18 points in the fourth, shooting 5-of-9 from the field. The 18 points were a season high for Thomas, who has scored in double figures in six of his eight appearances.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Donovan Mitchell (CLE): Donovan Mitchell recorded 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
item.description:
Donovan Mitchell recorded 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.

Like the other Cavaliers starters, Mitchell did not play at all in the fourth quarter. He and his backcourt partner, James Harden, had brutal first halves, scoring five points each while shooting a combined 2-of-13 from the field. They were more productive in the third quarter, but the damage was already done. The good news for fantasy managers is that Cleveland plays three more games this week.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Peyton Watson (CLE): Peyton Watson amassed 13 points (5-of-9 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Hornets.
item.description:

item.description:
Austin Reaves exploded for a season-high 43 points (14-of-27 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), five rebounds and four assists over 37 minutes to power the Lakers to a 121-116 win over the Pistons on Sunday.

No Luka Dončić, no problem. Reaves picked up the slack from a creation standpoint with the current MVP frontrunner sidelined by a back issue in this one. Dončić entered the contest averaging a league-best 40.1 points per game, leaving a significant void for the Lakers to fill. It wasn’t an issue for Reaves, who embraced the expanded offensive responsibilities, repeatedly getting to his spots and making Detroit pay in one-on-one situations from the mid-range. He poured in a team-high 19 first-half points to give Los Angeles a 13-point advantage at the break before tacking on 12 more in the third quarter alone. He drilled a crowd-silencing stepback three-pointer to give Los Angeles an eight-point lead in the final minute. It’s abundantly clear that his fantasy appeal rises exponentially whenever Dončić is out of the lineup. The Lakers continue their current road trip with a three-game week that includes showdowns against the Hawks, Bucks and Suns.

George Bissell

Jenkins erupted for a game-high 22 first-half points, shooting 7-of-9 from the floor and 6-of-7 from three-point range in just 13 minutes off the bench. He capped the spectacular half by burying his sixth triple just over one second before the buzzer, sending the crowd into halftime with one final highlight. His sublime effort provided a much-needed lift for Detroit on an off-night for Cade Cunningham, who was held to just - points. The 25-year-old backup point guard knocked down 8-of-14 from three-point range, eclipsing the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. He doesn’t offer a ton of fantasy appeal in a bench role, but that could change if he continues to shoot over 40 percent from downtown. item.title: [Recap] Stephen Curry (GSW): Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday.
item.description:
Stephen Curry exploded for a game-high 41 points (13-of-19 FGs, 10-of-10 FTs), six rebounds and six assists across 36 minutes to lead the Warriors to a 126-119 overtime win against the Magic on Saturday.

Curry’s sublime start to the year continued in this one as he topped the 40-point plateau for the second time in eight games. His signature sequence came in the final minute of regulation when he knocked down a three-pointer before sinking a pair of free throws and converting a go-ahead layup in the closing seconds. He added five points in overtime as Golden State was finally able to pull away for good. The 38-year-old legend has delivered first-round fantasy value so far, averaging 31.3 points through eight games. Are you not entertained? The Warriors are in line for a three-game week that features matchups against the Pelicans, Rockets and Spurs.

item.description:
Onyeka Okongwu (throat) is available to return to Saturday’s game against the Nets.

item.title: [Recap] Larry Nance (IND): Larry Nance Jr. shot 5-of-7 from the field in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets, scoring 15 points with two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers.
item.description:
Larry Nance Jr. shot 5-of-7 from the field in Saturday’s loss to the Nuggets, scoring 15 points with two rebounds, one assist and five three-pointers.

Nance was in a groove on Saturday, matching his career high with five three-pointers. The veteran forward/center needed just seven attempts to reach that mark, a welcome development after Nance began the season shooting 5-for-17 from deep. He still can’t be relied on in most fantasy leagues, but Nance played 13 minutes while fellow reserve Jay Huff (zero points, three rebounds) played 10 minutes.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Egor Dëmin (BKN): Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez said Saturday that Egor Dëmin (leg) is progressing in his recovery and will be re-evaluated next week.
item.description:
Nets head coach Jordi Fernandez said Saturday that Egor Dëmin (leg) is progressing in his recovery and will be re-evaluated next week.

Dëmin has missed the Nets’ last four games with a bruised right leg, and he’ll miss a few more before being re-evaluated. The second-year guard will miss games against the Hawks (Saturday) and the Mavericks (Sunday) before doctors re-evaluate his leg to assess his progress. Chaney Johnson has been the replacement in the starting lineup and should retain that role until Dëmin is allowed to return.
